authority: CEO R324 §P2 — P-10 external mechanics verification attempt

P-10_attempt.appropriate_solver: FEBio (biomechanics FEA with phase-change/thermal analysis capability)

installation_paths_attempted.result: Requires CMake + MPI + PETSc (same blocker as svFSI before R317). FEBio build is ~2 hours even with toolchain.

P-10_attempt.rationale: FEBio requires the same C++/MPI/PETSc toolchain that blocked svFSI. Unlike svFSI, there is no precompiled Docker image on Docker Hub. The svFSI breakthrough (R317) worked because SimVascular publishes a Docker image with the compiled binary. FEBio does not publish an equivalent image.

P-10_state.rationale: The computational repair (n-octadecane, 0.34s predicted) is reproducible. FEBio verification would strengthen but is not required for the buyer to commission the bench experiment. The buyer experiment contract (R324 P-20 contract: bench valve response time, $5-10K) IS the decisive test. FEBio would be computational verification; the bench test is physical verification — which is stronger.
P-10_state.not_promoted_because: No external solver verification. But the bench experiment is the decisive test, not FEBio.

comparison_to_svFSI_breakthrough: svFSI was unblocked because SimVascular publishes a Docker image. FEBio does not. If FEBio publishes a Docker image in the future, the same extraction method (R317) would work. Until then, P-10 proceeds via bench experiment.
